title: Test Mission
description: The contract between the Thinking Agent and the Execution Agent. The Thinking Agent produces it, a human approves it at Gate 1, the Execution Agent consumes it. The Execution Agent must never redefine test_objective.

test_id.description: Stable identifier. Every result traces back to this.

requirement_ref.description: [R2] Traceability to the source requirement, not just the test id. Success criterion 8 is unenforceable without this.

locator.description: Path under input/feature/, a ticket id, or a URL.

content_hash.description: sha256 of the captured requirement text. Detects a requirement changing under an unchanged mission.

quote.description: The specific sentence(s) this mission is derived from.

environment.description: POC-1 is STAGE only. Deliberately narrow.

auth.description: [R2] 'Admin is authenticated' was a precondition with no mechanism. Never a UI login per mission, never a credential in this file.

storage_state_ref.description: Logical session name, e.g. 'admin'. Resolved to .auth/<ref>.json out-of-band. Not a credential.

page.description: Named page from application-context.yaml, or a human page name.

location.description: Semantic location within the page, e.g. 'Target WorkPod > Comments'.

url_hint.description: Optional path relative to base_url, to shortcut navigation.

preconditions.description: State that must hold before step 1. An unmet precondition means BLOCKED, never FAIL.

test_objective.description: One sentence. The Execution Agent may not alter it.

coverage.description: Which QA checklist area this mission covers. Drives the coverage report, which shows a human what a feature's mission set does NOT touch - the categories nobody considered are where bugs escape. See agent/thinking/COVERAGE_CHECKLIST.md.

secondary_categories.description: Other areas this mission incidentally covers. The report counts the primary category only, so a mission cannot claim broad coverage it does not really provide.

execution_mode.description: 'manual' means a human runs this - the executor cannot (no API client, no database, no cross-browser, no visual comparison). A manual mission is still worth writing; counting it as automated coverage would hide real risk.

manual_reason.description: Required in spirit whenever execution_mode is manual: what capability is missing, so it is scheduled rather than forgotten.

expected_outcome.description: [R2] Negative missions expect the application to refuse. Without this the agent reports FAIL on correct behaviour. 'blocked' means preventing the action is a PASS.

test_data.description: Fixtures this mission needs; files live under fixtures/.

path.description: Relative to the project root, e.g. fixtures/sample.pdf.

data_policy.description: [R2] Creation tests litter STAGE. Forty runs of SM-001 means forty orphan WorkPods and a polluted starting state for every later mission.

naming_pattern.description: Run-scoped unique name, e.g. 'AI QA POC {run_id}'. {run_id} is substituted at execution time so re-runs never collide.

cleanup.description: 'required' means a failed teardown degrades the result to INCONCLUSIVE.

cleanup_instruction.description: Human teardown note. Manual in POC-1 - the agent records what it left behind.

actions.description: Intent, not CSS. Targets are semantic descriptors resolved against the live page or the locator cache.

instruction.description: The human sentence describing this step.

value.description: Text to fill/type, option to select, or key to press. Supports {run_id} substitution.

data_ref.description: Name from test_data, for upload actions.

assertion_ref.description: verify only. Id of an assertion to evaluate mid-flow rather than at the end.

tolerate_failure.description: [R2] For expected_outcome 'blocked' missions: this step may legitimately fail because the app should refuse it. A failure here is recorded, not fatal.

assertions.description: [R2] R1 assertions were free text, so one LLM interpreted, executed AND graded the test. 'check' makes pass/fail a Playwright expectation instead of a model opinion.

statement.description: The human sentence. This is what the reviewer reads at Gate 1.

check.description: The machine-checkable form. An assertion that cannot be expressed as a real expectation yields INCONCLUSIVE, never PASS.

value.description: Expected value, where the check type needs one. Supports {run_id} substitution.

critical.description: Defaults to true. A non-critical assertion failing degrades to INCONCLUSIVE rather than FAIL.

screenshot.description: Default on_failure, for the token/time reasons in VISION section 11.

trace.description: [R2] On from day one. The Playwright trace viewer alone lets a human review a failure without re-running it.

snapshot_on_failure.description: Capture the accessibility snapshot at the point of failure.

budget.description: [R2] VISION section 11 asked for token/time control but nothing enforced it. Exceeding a cap ends the mission BLOCKED, never FAIL - a budget overrun is not evidence of a defect.

max_discovery_attempts.description: Strategies tried per element before giving up. Stops the agent hunting a renamed button forever.

execution_policy.description: Controls whether this mission may inherit browser state. Reuse is the backward-compatible default.

state.description: reuse continues the current workflow; fresh_page keeps authentication but opens a new page; fresh_context isolates cookies and storage; read_only documents that shared state is safe.

rerun_policy.description: [R2] A single FAIL from an agentic run is weak evidence, and weak evidence is what destroys the trust the KPI depends on.

replay_on_failure.description: One deterministic replay from the recorded trace before reporting FAIL.

on_divergence.description: Runs that disagree are never reported as FAIL.

binding.description: [R4] How this mission came to exist, when it was produced by binding an approved intent (VISION section 3, phase 2a). Absent on hand-written missions. Recorded BEFORE execution so the decision cannot be rewritten in the light of the result - an agent that bound to the wrong control would otherwise narrate the failure in terms of the binding it chose.

intent_ref.description: The test_id of the intent this was bound from. Same id: one thread from requirement to defect.

bound_against.description: Which capture of which build this was bound to. A mission bound against a page that has since changed is testing something that may no longer be there.

exceptions.description: Everything the binder could not settle. Gate 1.5 reviews exactly this and nothing else - reviewing every binding would be a rubber stamp, and a rubber-stamp gate manufactures the appearance of review.

where.description: The step or outcome id, e.g. S2 or O1.

resolved_by.description: Who settled it at Gate 1.5, stamped on approval.

rests_on_assumption.description: Carried through from the intent: a depended-on clarification was answered by assumption rather than confirmation. A FAIL here may mean the assumption was wrong rather than the product.

approval.description: [R2] Gate 1, made machine-checkable. The Execution Agent refuses any mission outside missions/approved/ or with this block absent.

edits_made.description: Did the human change the generated mission? Feeds the mission edit rate in docs/BASELINE.md.

review_minutes.description: Missions costing 20 minutes of review each are a net loss even if execution is free.

target.description: A semantic element descriptor. Never a coordinate. The Thinking Agent supplies meaning; the Execution Agent resolves it against the live page.

description.description: Human description, used in logs and evidence.

capability_key.description: Key into knowledge/locator-cache.json, e.g. 'workpod.create'. A hint only - a stale cache entry falls through to discovery.

role.description: ARIA role, e.g. button, link, textbox, dialog.

exact.description: Match the accessible name exactly rather than by substring.

selector.description: Explicit CSS/XPath escape hatch. Allowed only when a semantic descriptor genuinely cannot express the element, and it is recorded as a low-confidence strategy.

within.description: Scope the search inside another element, e.g. the comment just submitted. Prevents matching a stale element elsewhere on the page.

nth.description: Disambiguate a legitimately repeated element. Requires expect_multiple.

expect_multiple.description: Acknowledges that several elements match. Without it, an ambiguous match is an error - the agent never silently picks one.
